industry.drivers: GST 2.0 rate cuts (Sep-2025) and income-tax relief lifted FY26 H2 volumes; CAFE norms tighten from Apr-2027 (LED, light-weighting); alloy-wheel penetration ~70% in 2W and ~40% in 4W (q4call); kit value per vehicle up to ~Rs22,000 (premium scooters) and ~Rs2.5 lakh (SUVs) on Uno Minda's full catalogue (q1deck p19, excl. EV parts).
industry.headwinds: West Asia conflict: crude, freight and aluminium prices up (aluminium at a record in Q4FY26; USD/INR above 95.5); state minimum wages up ~35% in Haryana under the new labour codes; the GST-boosted base from Q3FY27.

excluded.BHARATFORG: Earnings distorted: a Rs358 cr exceptional charge turned the Jun-2026 quarter into a Rs90 cr loss (exceptional items in three of the last four quarters), so its ~93x trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on depressed TTM EPS.
excluded.GABRIEL: No five-year history: Screener's P/E series starts in May-2024 (after Gabriel's restructuring).

peers.notes: The auto-component peer set used in the Samvardhana Motherson and Bosch initiations (same as-of date), with Uno Minda itself replaced by Motherson/Bosch. Tyre and battery makers are left out (different raw-material cycles). SCHAEFFLER (December year-end) has P/E history only from Feb-2023, MSUMI from Apr-2022 and ZFCVINDIA from May-2022: their medians cover the history available.

brokers.thesis: FY27 a 'defining growth year' (7 of 11 projects); 19%/20%/23% revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR FY26-28E; returns rise in FY28E as capacity ramps. Initiated 7-Jul-2026 at the same Rs1,406 (top auto-ancillary pick).
New products and capex to propel growth; ~17.7% revenue CAGR FY26-28E; kit value gains.
Revenue beat; EV, seating and sunroof expansion; 19%/22%/29% revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR FY26-28E (multiple raised from 36x).
Underperformance vs key client Maruti widened to -12.1% in Q1; growth moderating to ~20% (from 33% FY22-26) with flattish margins; 41x FY28E is rich.
Record quarter; strategic investments give growth visibility; 19% revenue CAGR FY26-29E.

brokers.method: P/E (initiation: 42x FY27E, near the 5-year average of 43x)
brokers.thesis: Initiation (10-Mar-2026): premium justified by a diversified, powertrain-agnostic portfolio, low margin volatility and high ROE; 17% revenue CAGR FY26-28E. Target raised to Rs1,500 after Q1 (aggregators).

street.notes: Nomura (Buy, reportedly Rs1,532 after Q1) could not be verified from a dated source: left out. Trendlyne put the average of six brokers' targets at Rs1,343 on 4-Aug-2026.

stockEvents: CMP Rs1,068 in the Emkay note
Q1FY27: revenue +26%, margin 10.3%; PV seating entry
moat: Breadth of catalogue and kit value
Strong
28 product lines, kit value per car up to ~Rs2.5 lakh on SUVs; 4W 45% / 2W 45% of revenue
Cross-selling lets it grow faster than vehicle production (FY26 +17% vs production +12%)
Japanese JV and licence partners
Strong
Toyoda Gosei, Tokai Rika, Denso Ten, Roki, Tachi-S, Aisin, Kyoraku, Inovance
Technology and OEM access, but partners own 30-51% of the best JVs and royalty/licence ties limit export rights
Scale in switches, horns, 2W lighting, alloy wheels
Moderate
Market leader in switches and horns; #3 in lighting; ~9.5 mn 2W and ~7 mn 4W wheel capacity after current projects
Leadership in mature lines; 4W lighting is a crowded field of global and Indian specialists
Pricing power
Weak
Commodity pass-through at cost with a quarter or half-year lag; ~40bp margin dilution in Q1FY27; EBITDA margin 10.7-12.3% since FY17
A classic tier-1: OEMs set the price; margins are stable but capped
Customer concentration
Moderate
Two customers above 10% of revenue in FY26; underperforming Maruti's volumes by ~10-12% (Emkay)
Diversified across OEMs, but exposed to share-of-business shifts
critiques: At 41x FY28E, Uno Minda is rich for ~20% growth with flattish margins; it is underperforming key client Maruti.
FY27 is a defining year: 7 of 11 projects ramp up; 45x FY28E is justified by growth and rising returns.
Premium valuations are justified: diversified, powertrain-agnostic, low margin volatility, high ROE.
Capex is front-loaded (Rs1,750 cr in FY27, ~Rs3,800 cr of projects); returns dip until FY28 ramp-up.
The Inovance EV-powertrain JV still needs Chinese approval under tightened technology-export rules.
